finding: Ordinance 023/PR/2018 verified in full official text (FAOLEX) as the governing association law: authorization regime, 3-month ministerial decision (art. 8), and foreign associations get only limited-term, renewable authorization (arts. 23-24). No successor law found; fees unpublished as claimed.

Official 2017 Journal Officiel shows the Interior Ministry citing the 1 July 1901 law as in force (with loi 19-60/1960 declaration regime) and confirms the fee schedule: 15,000 FCFA per association declaration. All claims verified.

cell_edits.Registration fee (USD): 500 CDF filing + 250 CDF publication (~$1); notary costs extra
cell_edits.Key local requirements: Foreign NGO: presidential authorization (decree) motioned by Justice Ministry, line-ministry approval, local representation in DRC, framework agreement with Planning Ministry; local office.
cell_edits.Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Presidential decree authorization for foreign NGO, local representation, framework agreement with Planning Ministry, local office

finding: Law 004/2001 (official text) sets the statutory fee at 500 CDF lodging + 250 CDF publication (~$1), not $100-300, and foreign NGOs need presidential authorization (decree) motioned by the Justice Ministry plus a framework agreement with the Planning Ministry, not 'Interior Ministry approval'.

Law 35/62 full text confirms the declaration regime and that foreign associations require presidential authorization on the report of the Interior Minister (arts. 25-27), null if unrequested (art. 26). The specific ONG law was adopted by the National Assembly 16 May 2025 and remained pending before the Senate as of the latest accessible source.

Full text of Lei 8/2012 (National Assembly gazette, 28 May 2012) confirms every cited article: escritura pública (art. 3.1), registry requiring 2 years existence and 10 members (art. 9.2), home-country gazette extract (art. 9.3-9.4), 15-day Justice Ministry decision (art. 9.5-9.6), and foreign-NGO partnership duty (art. 13).

The official presidential website hosts the 2017 associations law (loi-02-2017, 23 pages) and ICNL's legal library holds the separate 2017 law regulating foreign NGOs in Burundi, confirming the 2017 dual framework; fees and decision times remain unpublished as claimed.

NGO Act No 24 of 2002 (revised 2005, 2019) confirmed as governing law; the TANGO/ICNL toolkit lists the exact current fees (national TZS 115,000 + TZS 1,500 stamp duty; INGO USD 350 + TZS 4,500) and founder rules (local: 5+ all Tanzanians; INGO: 5+ incl. 2 Tanzanians) via the NIS portal.

Law 86-006/AF of 30 May 1986 verified in full on the official Ministry of Justice site: declaration with 15-day récépissé (art. 3) and prior Interior-Ministry authorization for foreign associations (art. 9-13). Decree 20-101/PR of 31 July 2020 on NGO agrément (accord de siège, local office, Comorian staff) confirmed.

cell_edits.Key local requirements: Foreign ONG: prior Interior Ministry authorization after MFA opinion (art. 37, Law 96-030); local legal representative and office; filings in French.
cell_edits.Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Prior Interior-Ministry authorization (after MFA opinion) for foreign ONG plus local representative/office; discretionary

finding: Law 96-030 (official MFA text) shows foreign ONGs need prior authorization from the Minister of the Interior after opinion of the Minister of Foreign Affairs (art. 37), not 'MFA accreditation'; the declaration + agrément regime (arts. 6-12) is as claimed.

cell_edits.Key local requirements: >=2 Malawian-citizen directors/trustees (s.20(2) NGO Act); local office; English filings; int'l NGOs need line-ministry approval letter/MoU.
cell_edits.Registration fee (USD): MK 250,000 (~$145) one-off NGORA fee + incorporation costs
cell_edits.Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): >=2 Malawian-citizen directors/trustees; mandatory partnership with a local NGO for international NGOs (2024 Regulations, NGORA guidelines 2026); line-ministry MoU

finding: NGORA's official site confirms the NGO (Amendment) Act 2022, the one-off MK 250,000 registration fee (~$145, not $50-100) and the >=2 Malawian-citizen directors/trustees rule (s.20(2)); the 'two-thirds Malawian board' claim is wrong, and international NGOs now face mandatory partnerships with local NGOs under the 2024 Regulations.

cell_edits.Main charitable entity types: Associations (Lei 8/91); Foundations (Lei 16/2018); Foreign NGO authorization (Decreto 55/98 via Ministry of Foreign Affairs); 2022 NGO law (OSFL) dropped from Parliament's agenda Apr 2023

finding: Lei 8/91, Lei 16/2018 and Decreto 55/98 (13 Oct, foreign-NGO authorization framework under Lei 8/91 art. 20) confirmed in current legislation lists; the 2022 OSFL NGO bill was dropped from Parliament's agenda in Apr 2023, so 'still pending' is outdated.

Lei 2/26 (NGO law, approved 22 Jan 2026, promulgated 19 Feb 2026, D.R. n.º 38 of 02/03/2026) verified in full: mandatory prior habilitação (art. 6), foreign-NGO registration documents (art. 8.4), and 180-day conformity deadline for existing NGOs (art. 35, i.e. by ~Sept 2026). Lei 6/12 remains the private-associations law.
